title: Extension by zero of a function C¹ on an open set whose nonzero set lies in a compact subset
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let K ⊆ U be compact, and let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be C¹ at every point of U. Assume every y ∈ U with h(y) ≠ 0 lies in K. Let g := 1_U·h be the extension of h|_U by zero, so g = h on U and g = 0 off U (Lean: U.indicator h). Then g is C¹ on ℝ^P, g has compact support, Dg(x) = Dh(x) for every x ∈ U, and Dg(x) = 0 for every x ∉ U.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ x ∈ U, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 h x) → (∀ y ∈ U, h y ≠ 0 → y ∈ K) → ContDiff ℝ 1 (U.indicator h) ∧ HasCompactSupport (U.indicator h) ∧ (∀ x ∈ U, fderiv ℝ (U.indicator h) x = fderiv ℝ h x) ∧ (∀ x ∉ U, fderiv ℝ (U.indicator h) x = 0)
